samples.question: The picture shows three square panels side by side on a plain background. Each panel is outlined by a frame of its own colour - one red frame, one green frame and one blue frame - and the frames are placed left to right in no fixed order. Inside every panel sit small round dots. Every dot in the picture is the same size and the same dark grey, no dot touches another dot, and each of the three panels contains exactly the same number of dots, so the panels use exactly the same amount of ink and differ only in where their dots sit. In exactly one panel the dots are spread evenly: each dot keeps roughly the same distance from its closest neighbour, so that panel shows no tight clump of dots and no wide empty patch. In each of the other two panels the dots are spread unevenly, gathering into crowded groups with bare ground between them. Judge a panel by the typical distance from a dot to its nearest neighbour: the evenly spread panel is the one where that typical nearest-neighbour distance is the largest, because its dots share the panel instead of huddling. The frame colours, the left-to-right order of the panels, the number of dots, the size of the dots and the total amount of ink carry no information about the answer. Which frame colour surrounds the panel whose dots are spread evenly? Answer red, green or blue.
